workflow_runs.display_title: Cause collect_output_until_deadline to return when session exits.

head_commit.message:
Release sessions lock before waiting for exit signal.

This separate commit addresses https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/6718#discussion_r2548248412

It combines exit_notify: Arc<Notify> and exit_status: Arc<AtomicBool>
into exit_status: Arc<ExitStatus> where ExitStatus is a new object
that handles threadsafe signaling and monitoring of the exit status
flag.

If the PTY process (wait_handle) observes that the child process
did exit then it calls ExitStatus::signal().

Polling is possible using ExitStatus::signal_received(), but that
is a fuzzy boolean (True or WasFalse): if the function returns
false then that only means it was very recently false.

One can wait for the signal to be received with
`ExitStatus::wait_for_exit_until(deadline)`, which returns true
if the process did exit and false if it didn't (but the deadline
was reached).

Note: the cheap and dirty "solution" to just drop the guard before
calling `wait_for_exited_until_deadline` meant that there would be
a race between the last check on the `exited` boolean and the
creation of the notify.notified() future, during which there was
a tiny window where we could miss the exit notify and wait till the
dealine for nothing. Wrapping all of this into its own class is much
cleaner and now we don't have such race.
